definitions.explanation: When a store has run out of a particular item and has none available. Often implies the item may be restocked later.

examples.japanese: {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません、{品切|しなぎ}れです。
その{商品|しょうひん}は{現在|げんざい}{品切|しなぎ}れ{中|ちゅう}です。
examples.english: That product is currently out of stock.

examples.japanese: {品切|しなぎ}れの{場合|ばあい}は{入荷|にゅうか}までお{待|ま}ちください。
examples.english: If it's out of stock, please wait until the next shipment arrives.

notes:
{品切|しなぎ}れ indicates that an item is temporarily unavailable because the store's stock has run out. It implies the item may be restocked, unlike {売|う}り{切|き}れ which emphasizes that all items were sold.

COMPOUND: {品|しな} (goods) + {切|き}れ (run out)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {品切|しなぎ}れ{中|ちゅう}: currently out of stock
- {品切|しなぎ}れになる: to go out of stock
- {品切|しなぎ}れの{場合|ばあい}: in case of being out of stock
- {品切|しなぎ}れ{商品|しょうひん}: out-of-stock item

COMPARISON WITH {売|う}り{切|き}れ:
- {品切|しなぎ}れ: focuses on inventory status (may be restocked)
- {売|う}り{切|き}れ: focuses on sales result (everything was sold, often implies it won't return)

USAGE:
Commonly seen on signs in stores and on e-commerce websites. Staff may say {品切|しなぎ}れです when apologizing to customers.
